lesson.title: Measuring and Time
lesson.summary: Length, mass, capacity, temperature, telling the time and reading a calendar.
learning_objectives: Choose the right tool to measure
Read o'clock, half past and quarter times

standards.text: Choose and use appropriate standard units to estimate and measure length, mass, temperature and capacity; tell and write the time to five minutes

blocks.markdown: Today we learn how to measure and how to tell the time.
blocks.say: Welcome back, number explorer! Today we measure and tell the time. How long is your pencil? How heavy is your bag? And what is the time right now? By the end you will know which tool to pick, read a clock, and use a calendar.

terms.meaning: To find out how big, heavy, long or hot something is.

blocks.markdown:
**Length** is how long. **Mass** is how heavy. **Capacity** is how much a container holds.

We use a ruler, scales and a measuring jug.
blocks.say: We measure things to say how big, how heavy or how much. Length tells us how long or tall something is, and we use a ruler. Mass tells us how heavy something is, and we use scales. Capacity tells us how much a container holds, and we use a measuring jug. Each one has its own tool.

blocks.alt: A ruler measures length. Scales measure mass. A jug measures capacity.
blocks.caption: A ruler measures length. Scales measure mass. A jug measures capacity.

question.prompt: Which tool measures how heavy something is?

blocks.markdown: Length: centimetres. Mass: grams and kilograms. Capacity: millilitres and litres.
blocks.say: In school we often use centimetres for length. A pencil is about fifteen centimetres long. We use grams and kilograms for mass. A big bag of rice is one kilogram. And millilitres and litres for capacity. A bottle of water holds about one litre.

blocks.markdown:
**Temperature** is how hot or cold. We measure it in degrees Celsius with a thermometer.

The higher the red line, the hotter it is.
blocks.say: Temperature tells us how hot or cold something is. We use a thermometer. Look at the red line. When it is cold, the line is low. When it is hot, the line rises. A cold winter day in England can be near zero degrees. A summer day in Pakistan can be forty degrees or more. Temperature is measured in degrees Celsius.

blocks.say: Remember. Length is how long, mass is how heavy, capacity is how much it holds, and temperature is how hot or cold. Each one has its own tool.

blocks.markdown:
The short hand shows the **hour**. When the long hand points to 12, it is **o'clock**.

Long hand on 12, short hand on 3: three o'clock.
blocks.say: A clock has two hands. The short hand is the hour hand. The long hand is the minute hand. When the long hand points straight up to the twelve, it is an o'clock time. The short hand tells us which hour. Here the short hand points to three. So it is three o'clock.

scenes.caption: Long hand on 12: o'clock.
scenes.say: The long hand points straight up at twelve. That means o'clock.

scenes.caption: It is 3 o'clock.
scenes.say: The short hand points to three. So the time is three o'clock.

question.explanation: Long hand on 12 and short hand on 7 is 7 o'clock.

blocks.markdown:
**Half past**: the long hand points to 6, and the short hand is half way between two numbers.

Half past 3 is 3:30.
blocks.say: Half past means the long hand has gone half way round the clock. It points straight down to the six. The short hand is half way between two hours. Here it is half way between three and four. So it is half past three.

scenes.caption: Long hand on 6: half past.
scenes.say: The long hand points straight down to six. That is half way round.

scenes.caption: It is half past 3.
scenes.say: The short hand sits between three and four. It is half past three.

sub_lessons.title: Quarter past, quarter to and five minutes

blocks.text: Stop 1: Quarter past and quarter to

blocks.markdown:
**Quarter past**: long hand on 3. **Quarter to**: long hand on 9.

Quarter past 3 is 3:15. Quarter to 4 is 3:45.
blocks.say: A quarter is one of four equal parts. A clock can be split into four quarters. Quarter past means the long hand has moved a quarter of the way round. It points to the three. Quarter to means it still has a quarter of the way to go. It points to the nine. Quarter past three is three fifteen. Quarter to four is three forty-five.

blocks.markdown:
Count in **fives** round the clock: the 1 is 5 minutes, the 2 is 10 minutes, the 3 is 15 minutes.

Long hand on 2 is ten past.
blocks.say: The minute hand jumps in fives. When it points to one, that is five minutes past. Two is ten minutes past. Count in fives around the clock. Five, ten, fifteen, twenty, twenty-five, thirty. Thirty minutes is half an hour. Here the minute hand is on two. That is ten past three.

blocks.text: Stop 1: Days of the week and months

blocks.markdown:
There are seven days in a **week** and twelve months in a **year**.

Muslims also use the Islamic calendar, which includes Ramadan.
blocks.say: A calendar helps us keep track of time. There are seven days in a week. Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday and Sunday. There are twelve months in a year. January, February, March and on to December. Some months have thirty days, some thirty-one, and February has only twenty-eight. Muslims also follow the Islamic months, like Ramadan, which move around the year.

blocks.alt: A calendar shows days, weeks and months.
blocks.caption: A calendar shows days, weeks and months.

question.prompt: How many days are in one week?
question.explanation: There are 7 days in a week.

blocks.markdown:
Count days on the calendar to find out how long until an event.

Wednesday to Saturday is 3 days.
blocks.say: Let us use a calendar. Find today's date. What day of the week is it? How many days until the weekend? Count the days on the calendar. If today is Wednesday, Thursday is one, Friday is two, Saturday is three. Three days until Saturday. Calendars help us plan for birthdays, trips and Eid.

blocks.caption: Counting days on a calendar.
blocks.say: Count the days on the calendar, like Wednesday to Saturday.
